20: Bob Proctor continues his foreword with a personal origin story. When he first received the book, he was a confused, unhappy, and broke 26-year-old sitting in a fire hall in a Toronto suburb, with virtually no formal education and no business experience. His mental focus was perpetually on what he lacked and why he couldn't achieve his dreams. Hill's work shifted his mindset to focus on what he could do, causing him to search for how to accomplish things rather than why he couldn't. Through repeated reading of each chapter, Proctor developed a healthy respect for his potential and capabilities. He now owns multiple prosperous companies operating worldwide (The LifeSuccess Group of Companies), focused on helping people understand and develop their potential—the same area Hill dedicated his life to. Proctor formed the habit of reading a few lines daily from the book and concludes that whatever challenge he faces, the solution will be found in its pages. He specifically recommends reading the 'Persistence' chapter daily for 30 days, at least twice a year. He describes traveling to Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, to speak at the Napoleon Hill Foundation's international conference, where the Prime Minister of Malaysia received the Napoleon Hill Award.
